capabilities: Sync a vault bidirectionally with a WebDAV server (upload, download, delete)
Keep both conflict copies or keep the newest version
Archive trashed files remotely as an append-only backup
Back up and restore encrypted plugin configs and Copilot keychain keys
Trigger syncs manually, on an interval, at startup, or after editing stops
disambiguation: Not the rsync file tool; it syncs an Obsidian vault over the WebDAV protocol only.
extras: WebDAV password is stored in plain text in the plugin's data.json; desktop only, mobile unverified; no cross-device lock, so avoid editing the same file on two devices at once.
motivation: The author wanted free, lightweight two-way sync that uses only WebDAV and does not depend on proprietary services such as S3, Dropbox, or OneDrive.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to keep a vault in sync through a self-hosted WebDAV server without relying on proprietary cloud services.

requires.name: WebDAV server (PROPFIND, PUT, GET, MKCOL, DELETE, HTTP Basic Auth)

summary: Two-way WebDAV sync plugin that mirrors a vault to any standard WebDAV server, with an append-only trash archive and encrypted plugin-config backup.
